title: Home Wreckers
cn: 第 20 集 · 房屋破坏者
novel:
Ted bought a house. It was, everyone agreed, a [[wreck|wreck]] — a [[fixer-upper|fixer-upper]] that looked more like a [[bargain|bargain]] gone wrong. The roof leaked, the floors creaked, and something lived in the walls.

"You [[overpaid|overpay]]," Barney said. "Tear it down and start again."

But Ted saw [[potential|potential]]. He would [[renovate|renovate]] it with his own hands, turn it into a home worth keeping.

Meanwhile, Robin and Don grew [[serious|serious]]. They shared coffee at five in the morning, laughed over bad news, and forgot to be [[rivals|rival]]. Robin was, for once, not pretending.

Ted's mother announced she was marrying her [[longtime|longtime]] friend. Ted felt a strange [[mixture|mixture]] of joy and [[loss|loss]]. The parent he had known was becoming someone new.

He stood in the [[gutted|gut]] living room, dust in his hair, and smiled. Some things fell apart so better things could be built. His mother had found love. Robin had found a partner. And Ted, surrounded by [[rubble|rubble]], had found a project that might one day become a home.

overpay.en: to pay more than something is worth

potential.en: the ability to become something better

renovate.en: to repair and improve an old building

loss.en: the sad feeling when someone changes or leaves

gut.en: to remove the inside of a building

rubble.en: broken pieces of stone and brick
